lens: Markets snapped risk-off (VIX ~19.5, Dow -1.5%, WTI +7% to ~$85) but the deal machine kept filing: Dominion and NextEra put their utility mega-merger to proxy (Goldman, JPMorgan / Lazard, BofA), Grant Thornton agreed to take CBIZ private for $5B with a live go-shop, Expand Energy bought Twin Eagle for $1.25B, and a PBT royalty-trust roll-up and a Wynnchurch/Luxfer take-private round out a filing-heavy day — signed processes that keep secure rooms busy regardless of the tape.

stories.headline: Goldman and JPMorgan advise Dominion Energy’s board as NextEra files its stock-and-cash merger proxy (Lazard, BofA for NextEra)
stories.why_it_matters: Dominion Energy (D) and NextEra Energy (NEE) filed a definitive joint proxy/prospectus (DEFM14A, Jul 28) for their merger, in which each Dominion share converts to 0.8138 NextEra shares plus a pro-rata portion of an aggregate $360M one-time cash payment (implied roughly $73–$76/share at signing). The filing names Goldman Sachs and J.P. Morgan as financial advisers to the Dominion board (Annex E / Annex F fairness opinions), with Lazard and BofA Securities advising NextEra (Annex C / Annex D). A mega-cap utility merger heading to dual shareholder votes runs one of the most document- and regulatory-intensive diligence processes in the market.
stories.suggested_action: Engage Goldman’s and JPMorgan’s power & utilities coverage on Dominion/NextEra — a four-adviser mega-merger advancing to a vote runs concentrated confirmatory, regulatory (FERC/state PUC), and integration diligence a secure room is built for.

deal_clock.event: Dominion & NextEra file DEFM14A (0.8138 exchange ratio + $360M cash pool)

stories.headline: Goldman advises CBIZ as Grant Thornton Advisors agrees to take it private for ~$5B; Evercore, JPMorgan among a deep buy-side roster
stories.why_it_matters: Grant Thornton Advisors (backed by New Mountain Capital) agreed to acquire CBIZ (CBZ) in an all-cash take-private at $55.00/share (~$5B EV, ~54% premium to the 30-day VWAP), with a go-shop through Aug 27 and CBIZ’s Benefits & Insurance segment to be carved out into a standalone New Mountain-backed company. The release names Goldman Sachs advising CBIZ (sell-side); Deutsche Bank as lead adviser to Grant Thornton with J.P. Morgan, BMO, BofA Securities, RBC and UBS also buy-side; and Evercore advising New Mountain on the B&I carve-out. A large take-private plus a simultaneous carve-out runs two overlapping diligence tracks.
stories.suggested_action: Open with Goldman (CBIZ), JPMorgan/BofA/UBS (Grant Thornton), or Evercore (the B&I carve-out) — a $5B take-private with a go-shop and a concurrent carve-out is a multi-room, multi-party diligence process through Q4.

deal_clock.event: Grant Thornton agrees to acquire CBIZ at $55.00/share (~$5B EV)

stories.headline: JPMorgan advises Blackbeard on the ~$2.2B combination of Permian Basin Royalty Trust with US Land Guild
stories.why_it_matters: Permian Basin Royalty Trust (PBT) filed a Form 425 (Jul 29) on its ~$2.2B combination with US Land Guild to form PBT Land and Minerals, with PBT unitholders taking ~59% and Blackbeard/affiliates ~41% pro forma. The release names RBC Capital Markets and J.P. Morgan as financial advisers to Blackbeard (buy-side), with Stephens advising SoftVest. A royalty-trust roll-up into a new operating company runs asset, title, and reserve diligence toward a unitholder vote.
stories.suggested_action: Engage JPMorgan’s energy/A&D coverage on the PBT combination — a royalty-to-operating-company conversion runs concentrated reserve and title diligence into the vote.

deal_clock.event: PBT files Form 425 on ~$2.2B combination with US Land Guild

stories.headline: PJT Partners advises Expand Energy on its $1.25B acquisition of Twin Eagle from Five Point; Lazard advises the seller
stories.why_it_matters: Expand Energy (EXE) agreed to acquire natural-gas marketer Twin Eagle Holdings from Five Point Infrastructure for $1.25B cash, adding ~14 Bcf/d of marketing capacity to build what the parties call North America’s leading integrated natural gas company. The release names PJT Partners as exclusive adviser to Expand (buy-side) and Lazard as adviser to Twin Eagle/Five Point (sell-side). A midstream/marketing acquisition runs contract, credit, and counterparty diligence to close.
stories.suggested_action: Reach out to PJT (Expand) and Lazard (Five Point) on Twin Eagle — a gas-marketing carve-out from a sponsor runs contract and counterparty diligence a secure room organizes.

deal_clock.event: Expand Energy agrees to acquire Twin Eagle for $1.25B

stories.headline: Lazard advises Wynnchurch on its $17.37/share take-private of Luxfer; Deutsche Bank advises Luxfer
stories.why_it_matters: A Wynnchurch Capital affiliate agreed to take Luxfer Holdings (LXFR), a materials-technology maker, private in an all-cash deal at $17.37/share. The release names Deutsche Bank Securities advising Luxfer (sell-side) and Lazard advising Wynnchurch (buy-side). A cross-listed (US/UK) sponsor take-private runs confirmatory diligence and scheme/merger mechanics toward close.
stories.suggested_action: Engage Lazard (Wynnchurch) on the Luxfer take-private — a sponsor buyout of a dual-jurisdiction materials maker runs confirmatory and regulatory diligence a data room supports.

deal_clock.event: Wynnchurch agrees to take Luxfer private at $17.37/share

stories.headline: Guggenheim advises Katapult on its merger with CCFI/Aaron’s entities as a supplemental proxy sharpens the fairness disclosures
stories.why_it_matters: Katapult Holdings (KPLT) filed a Form 425 (Jul 27) supplementing the fairness-opinion disclosures ahead of the stockholder vote on its merger with CCF Holdings/Aaron’s Intermediate Holdings (agreement dated Dec 11, 2025). The filing attributes the financial analyses to Guggenheim Securities, confirming Guggenheim as Katapult’s adviser delivering the fairness opinion (sell-side). A fintech/lease-to-own merger heading to a vote runs concentrated confirmatory diligence.
stories.suggested_action: Note Guggenheim’s role on Katapult ahead of the vote — a supplemented proxy signals a live process worth a light-touch outreach on secure diligence support.

deal_clock.event: Katapult files Form 425 supplementing fairness disclosures

stories.headline: Jefferies, Guggenheim and UBS act as placement agents as Synlogic and Caldera merge with a $278M private placement
stories.why_it_matters: Synlogic (SYBX) agreed to a reverse merger with private biotech Caldera Therapeutics, with the combined company led by Caldera and a concurrent upsized $278M private placement from healthcare institutions (Bain Capital Life Sciences, TCGX, Atlas Venture, venBio, Omega, Blackstone Multi-Asset, others). The release names Lucid Capital Markets advising Synlogic and Jefferies, TD Cowen, Guggenheim, UBS and LifeSci Capital as placement agents to Caldera. A biotech reverse merger plus a large PIPE runs parallel diligence and disclosure workstreams.
stories.suggested_action: Reach out to Jefferies/Guggenheim/UBS healthcare coverage on Synlogic/Caldera — a reverse merger with a $278M PIPE runs concurrent diligence tracks a secure room keeps organized.

deal_clock.event: Synlogic & Caldera announce merger + $278M private placement

stories.headline: Risk-off snap-back: Dow -1.5%, VIX jumps ~7% to ~19.5, WTI spikes ~7% to ~$85; advisory names sink (GS -4%, EVR -10%)
stories.why_it_matters: US equities reversed lower Jul 29 — Dow -1.5% (51,963), S&P -0.75% (7,373), Nasdaq -1.05% (24,615), Russell 2000 -0.85% — with the VIX jumping ~7% to ~19.5 and the 10Y ticking up to ~4.63%. WTI crude spiked ~7% to ~$84.85, unwinding the prior day’s drop. Advisory stocks were hit hard: Goldman -4.1%, Morgan Stanley -2.9%, Jefferies -3.3%, Lazard -3.8%, and Evercore -10.3% (earnings-driven). A sharper tape doesn’t stop signed processes — but it is exactly when clients value certainty of execution.
stories.suggested_action: Frame outreach around execution certainty — with volatility snapping back to ~19.5 and energy re-pricing, deal teams want signed processes to stay on schedule; room readiness is what protects the timeline.

talking_point.quote: The tape snapped risk-off today — VIX back up near 20, crude spiking 7%, the advisory names all red — but the signings didn’t blink: Dominion and NextEra filed their utility mega-merger proxy, Grant Thornton agreed to take CBIZ private for $5 billion with a live go-shop, and Expand Energy bought Twin Eagle for $1.25B. A choppier backdrop is exactly when clients want certainty their signed processes stay on schedule — how are you thinking about room readiness on the deals you’re carrying into August?
talking_point.use_with: M&A, sponsors, utilities/energy, and professional-services coverage teams (esp. Goldman, JPMorgan, Evercore, Lazard, PJT, Guggenheim)
talking_point.context: Pairs a Jul 29 risk-off read with a dense filing/signing cycle — a natural way to open a room-readiness conversation as deals push toward August milestones.

items.bank: Goldman Sachs and Evercore (per Reuters-sourced reporting; wire attribution, not a company disclosure)
items.lead: PayPal’s board rejected a $60.50/share (~$53B) take-private bid from Stripe and Advent International as inadequate; the company says it’s pursuing a standalone turnaround but remains open to evaluating opportunities. A live, unsolicited-approach / defense situation.
items.why_unverified: Bid and rejection are Reuters “sources say” reporting; PayPal has not formally disclosed a bid or process, and Stripe/Advent have not commented. Board advisers named only via trade press.

items.lead: Devon Energy is weighing a potential ~$4B sale of its Eagle Ford and Powder River shale assets as part of a portfolio streamlining, according to Bloomberg.
items.why_unverified: Bloomberg “sources familiar” report; no company confirmation and no adviser named.

items.company: Associated British Ports (private; CPP Investments & OMERS, ~64%)
items.lead: Adani Ports (APSEZ) is evaluating an early-stage bid for a controlling ~64% stake in Associated British Ports, the UK’s largest port operator, in a deal that could value ABP above £10B.
items.why_unverified: Reported as “early-stage” discussions that may not lead to a formal offer; APSEZ declined to comment and the Canadian pension owners have not confirmed a sale. No adviser named.

items.lead: Valmet’s board announced a company-confirmed strategic review evaluating a potential separation of its two segments into two standalone Nasdaq Helsinki-listed companies — a demerger/spin evaluation rather than an outright sale.
items.why_unverified: Company-confirmed inside-information release, but explicitly states no guarantee of any transaction; no adviser named, and it is a structural separation, not a sale to a buyer.

items.why_unverified: First reported by Axios citing sources; no named adviser and no formal process disclosed. A second sale attempt after a prior effort was shelved.
